This application, under Section 482 of Cr.P.C, has been filed for quashment of FIR in Crime No. 46 of 2022 registered at Police Station Ashoknagar Mahila Thana, District Ashok Nagar for offences under Sections 498A, 506, 504, and 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

It is stated that an amount of Rupees 25 lakhs was spent in marriage, out of which Rupees 15 lakhs were given in cash.

sentences.text: Accordingly, she was instructed to bring an amount of Rupees 25 lakhs and a vehicle, otherwise she was instructed not to come back to her matrimonial house.
When respondent No. 5 narrated the incident to her husband Vineet Sharma, he also instructed that she should act as per the dictates of his parents.

After 15 days when respondent No.5 went to her parental home, then parents of respondent No. 5 tried to persuade the husband, mother-in-law, and father-in-law of respondent No. 5 by clarifying that they do not have any money but, in order to save family reputation, they did not lodge any FIR.
Thereafter, on 06.07.2021, when father-in-law of respondent No. 5 came to Ashok Nagar to bring her back, then again he demanded an amount of Rupees 25 lakhs and a four-wheeler vehicle.

Again,
parents of respondent No. 5 tried to persuade the father-in-law of respondent No. 5 that they do not have the money.
Then with great difficulty, father-in-law of respondent No. 5 took her back to her matrimonial house.
As soon as she reached her matrimonial house, mother-in- law of respondent No. 5 started abusing her and scolded her as to why she has not brought 25 lakhs and the four-wheeler vehicle.
When respondent No. 5 replied that it is beyond the financial capacity of her father, then father-in-law and mother-in-law started assaulting her, and with great difficulty,
respondent No. 5 went to her room.

When she narrated the incident to her husband, he also NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:7929 assaulted her and insisted that she should fulfil the demand from her parents, otherwise he would divorce her.
Thereafter, it is alleged that on trivial issues, father-in-law, mother-in-law, as well as applicant Nos. 1 and 2 started harassing her mentally, and on trivial issues they used to assault her.
Thereafter, respondent No. 5 called her father and brother.

When her parents came to her matrimonial house, father-in-law and mother-in-law of respondent No. 5 started pressurising them to take respondent No. 5 back to the parental home because she does not do any household work, and also insisted that she should come back only when the demand is fulfilled.
At that time, applicant No. 2 also said that respondent No. 5 should go from the matrimonial house.
Thereafter, respondent No. 5 came back to her parental home at Ashok Nagar along with her father and brother.

It is alleged that thereafter, mother-in-law,
father-in-law and her husband along with applicants used to make telephonic calls and used to abuse her and demand dowry.
It is alleged that husband of respondent No. 5 was working on the post of Assistant Manager in HDFC Bank, Branch Ashok Nagar.
On 15.09.2021, husband of respondent No. 5 came to her parental home and again demanded dowry of Rupees 25 lakhs.
With great difficulty, husband of respondent No. 5 agreed to take her back to her matrimonial house and they started living in Sony Colony, Ashok Nagar.

It is alleged that in Sony Colony also,
mother-in-law, father-in-law, and applicants came and assaulted her and demanded dowry, as a result of which respondent No. 5 fell ill.
However, she was not got treated by her husband, and he left her.
Ultimately, she called her parents to get her treated.
It is alleged that thereafter she has been ousted by her father-in-law, mother-in-law, and husband from her matrimonial house, and they have kept the entire Stridhan with them.
She was ousted from her matrimonial house in the clothes which she was wearing.
A threat was also extended that unless and until Rupees 25 lakhs NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:7929 and one four-wheeler vehicle is not given, they would not keep respondent No. 5.

On 9.4.2022, father-in-law, mother-in-law, and husband of respondent No. 5 raised a demand and misbehaved with her, and it is alleged that since then, they are frequently making telephonic calls and harassing her physically and mentally and demanding Navneet Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11054717/

sentences.text: Accordingly, FIR was lodged.
4. From a plain reading of the FIR, it is clear that general and omnibus allegations have been made against the applicants.

Specific allegations have been made against father-in-law, mother-in-law,
and husband of respondent No. 5.

But so far as applicant No. 1 and 2, who are the younger brother-in-law (Devar) and sister-in-law (Nanad) of respondent No. 5 are concerned, it is merely alleged that they also demanded money and harassed her mentally and assaulted her on certain occasions, but the details of the dates on which such criminal acts were done by the applicants have not been clarified.
It is a well-established principle of law that to prosecute near and dear relatives of husband of the complainant, allegations must be clear and specific.
General and omnibus allegations are not sufficient to compel the near and dear relatives of the husband to face the ordeal of trial.

5. The Supreme Court in the cases of Kansraj Vs. State of Punjab reported in (2000) 5 SCC 207,
Monju Roy Vs. State of West Bengal reported in (2015) 13 SCC 693, Chandralekha & Ors. v. State of Rajasthan & Anr. reported in 2013 (1) UC 155, K. Subba Rao and others Vs. State of Telangana reported in (2018) 14 SCC 452, Preeti Gupta Vs. State of Jharkhand reported in AIR 2010 SC 3363,
Neelu Chopra and another Vs. Bharti reported in (2009) 10 SCC 184 and Geeta Mehrotra Vs. State of U.P. reported in (2012) 10 SCC 741 has held that the near and dear relatives NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:7929 of the deceased should not be compelled to face the ordeal of trial unless and until there are specific allegations against them.

sentences.text: 6. Considering the totality of facts and circumstances of the case coupled with the vague allegations made against applicants, this Court is of the considered opinion that the allegations which have been made against applicants are not sufficient to compel the applicants to face the ordeal of criminal prosecution.

7. Accordingly, the FIR in Crime No. 46 of 2022 registered at Police Station Ashoknagar Mahila Thana, District Ashok Nagar, and the charge sheet filed after completion of investigation and consequential criminal proceedings against applicants namely Navneet Sharma and Shraddha Sharma are hereby quashed.
8. Application succeeds and is hereby allowed.

(G. S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE (and)
